rule: SI-115 (CONSTRAINTS.md); user decision 2026-10-28: scoring of the pilot may be mixed across the workstation and JHPCE
meaning: Score rows made on the workstation and score rows made on JHPCE with the LISI seed fixed (cluster/jhpce/score_array_fixed_seed.sh) may share one rule input. scripts/prereg_rules.py (refuse_unknown_scorer_sites) accepts that mix only if every row is a workstation row (cpu_model listed below, no score_site) or a JHPCE row carrying score_site, lisi_random_device and lisi_preload_sha256 exactly as below, and only while identity_check names an intact file (SHA-256) whose result is 'every column identical on at least 3 latents'. Any other mix (JHPCE rows without the fixed seed, another CPU, rows without these columns) is refused. The five PROVENANCE_COLS must still agree across the whole input (scorer commit, dirty flag, SIMD width, NUMBA_CPU_NAME, package versions).

workstation.why: RDRAND and RDSEED on this CPU always return 0xffffffff, so scib 1.1.7's knn_graph helper (mt19937 seeded from std::random_device) always scores the same half of the cells for iLISI and cLISI (experiments/lisi_jhpce_investigation_20261028/lisi_jhpce_investigation_20261028.md section 1, branch lisi-jhpce-investigation@ed280a2).

jhpce_fixed_seed.preload_source: fixed_random_device.cpp, branch lisi-jhpce-investigation@ed280a2, built with g++ 11.4 on JHPCE (command in that report, section 2)
jhpce_fixed_seed.nodes: Slurm feature znver2 (AMD EPYC 7702, Zen 2), the type of the 20-latent match check

limits: Equality was shown for the latents of the identity check only; it rests on the preload making the JHPCE draw equal to the workstation's stuck RDRAND value.
If the workstation's RDRAND state ever changes (firmware, other machine), every workstation LISI value changes by about 0.005 and this record no longer describes the workstation rows.
Non-Zen 2 JHPCE nodes (AVX-512) were not tested; the scoring jobs request znver2 only.
